relations.subject: Martin Haug
relations.evidence: in 1848 he entered the University of Tübingen, where he studied oriental languages, especially Sanskrit.

relations.subject: Martin Haug
relations.evidence: He afterwards attended lectures at the University of Göttingen

relations.subject: Martin Haug
relations.evidence: and in 1854 settled as Privatdozent at the University of Bonn.

relations.subject: Martin Haug
relations.evidence: In 1856, he moved to Heidelberg University, where he assisted Bunsen in his literary undertakings.

relations.subject: Martin Haug
relations.role: superintendent of Sanskrit studies and professor of Sanskrit
relations.evidence: In 1859, he accepted an invitation to India, where he became superintendent of Sanskrit studies and professor of Sanskrit in Poona.

relations.subject: Martin Haug
relations.role: professor of Sanskrit and comparative philology
relations.evidence: he was called to the Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München as professor of Sanskrit and comparative philology in 1868.

relations.subject: Martin Haug
